List markets with optional filters and a sortable order.

Discovery defaults are tuned so customers see *something to buy* without
having to opt in: pass `has_data=true` and `sort_by=top` (the frontend
does this by default) and the empty 99.8% of the catalogue is filtered
out, with the highest-volume buyable markets at the top.

post.description:
Cost preview for a single market + date range.

Mirrors the catalogue series estimate but for one market. Pro-rates the
full `trade_count` / `orderbook_count` by the overlap between the
customer's window and the market's `[data_from, data_to]`, so picking
"Custom: Jan 25 12:00–12:30" on a market with 1h of data shows roughly
half the cost, not the full-market cost.

Returns `in_range=false` when there's no overlap, so the UI can disable
the add-to-cart button without a second round-trip.

get.description: One market's crawlable metadata, or 404.

List recent trades from the live tail. NOT the historical archive.

⚠️ **This endpoint queries Postgres `trades`, which holds only the recent
live tail — not the 217M-row historical archive.** Historical trades live in
R2 and are served by `GET /v1/download/trades` (small windows) or
`POST /v1/exports` (anything large). A market can therefore return `[]` here
and still have thousands of rows available to download.

That is not hypothetical: it confused a paying customer on 2026-09-02, who
reasonably read an empty list as "no data" for a market holding 15,708
trades. When we can detect that mismatch we now say so on the response:

    X-Data-Source: live-tail
    X-Historical-Trades: 15708
    X-Historical-Hint: /v1/download/trades or POST /v1/exports

The body stays a bare array so existing clients are unaffected.

`market_id` is the customer-facing markets.id. We translate to the
underlying outcome token ids before querying — see market_keys.py.

get.description: Get most recent trades across all markets.

Download trades data in CSV, Parquet, or JSON format.

`market_id` is the customer-facing markets.id. We translate to the trades
table's outcome token ids (both YES and NO) so the customer gets a single
file combining both sides of the market — see app/market_keys.py.

Data source: R2 daily Parquet files (217M rows, 2024-02 → present),
indexed by data_catalog. The Postgres `trades` table only carries the
live-tail captured by the realtime indexer — historical reads must go to
R2 or the customer sees an almost-empty file.

Download OHLCV data in CSV, Parquet, or JSON format.

Like /trades, OHLCV is keyed by outcome token id. We resolve the
markets.id to its clob_token_ids and IN-filter so both outcomes ship.

Download orderbook snapshots.

Reads from the orderbook_by_market R2 layout: one Parquet file per
market per day. Selecting the right files by condition_id means we
never scan rows for other markets.

FREE-tier preview: a delayed **top-of-book** projection (best bid/ask/mid/
spread) of orderbook snapshots — never full depth. Deliberately non-valuable:
bounded to the last `FREE_TIER.depth_days`, delayed `FREE_TIER.delay_hours`,
and capped at the Free monthly export. For real-time or full-depth data, buy
the `orderbook` product.

Not priced/charged: served free WITHIN the envelope (counts against the Free
monthly cap), refused **429** past the cap, **400** outside the window. Every
serve is logged `status='free_tier'` so `free_month_bytes` stays correct — the
delivery + the cap-accounting land together (the discipline §9.55 requires).

get.description:
Download derivatives data for a Deribit / Lyra / Aevo / Delta series.

Reads directly from R2 via the data_catalog index — every record
carries its own `instrument_name` (e.g. BTC-29DEC23-50000-C) plus
parsed underlying/expiry/strike/option_type, so no token resolution
is needed.

Supported `data_type` values:
  - `trades` — raw trade fills with price, size, direction, IV, mark,
               index, etc. Available for both options and futures series.
  - `greeks` — Black-76 delta/gamma/vega/theta/rho computed per trade
               using the IV the venue reported at trade time. Options
               series only (futures don't have greeks).

`instrument_prefix` narrows to a specific expiry/strike via PyArrow
predicate pushdown — a quant pulling 'BTC May 29 calls only' isn't
billed for puts.

get.description:
Discovery feed for the raw event-granular L2 capture streams — the
unbackfillable prediction-market moat data. Public-ish (like /v1/series):
lists each dataset with its venue, pricing, and the download path. Pull the
bytes with `GET /v1/download/raw?data_type=<data_type>&start=&end=&format=`.

Cost preview for a raw-capture stream + date range — NO charge, no download.

The raw datasets feed advertises only a $/MB rate, so a customer couldn't
see a total before pulling the bytes. This sums the record counts in the
window (paginated — never silently truncated) and prices the `shape=raw`
download exactly as `/v1/download/raw` would (`_cost_for`, capped at `limit`).
`shape=normalized` is charged on the actual serialized bytes at download time
and will differ. Public-ish (like `/raw/datasets`) since it never spends.

Accepts the series id (`polymarket:l2-delta-tape`) as well as the catalog
data_type — see `resolve_raw_identifier`.

parameters.name: limit

schema.description: Row cap to price against — mirrors the /v1/download/raw limit.

get.description:
Download the RAW event-granular L2 capture tape for prediction markets
(Hyperliquid HIP-4 / Polymarket CLOB / Polymarket US) — the unbackfillable
moat data nobody else sells.

Stored as zstd-NDJSON on R2, many per-flush objects per day. With
`shape=raw` (default) each record is `{"recv_ts": <ms>, "frame": <raw venue
frame text>}` and the customer parses `frame` themselves — the verbatim tape,
no normalization baked in. With `shape=normalized` we flatten the frames at
read time into a queryable per-level depth table (no extra storage, no new
service); charged on the real bytes shipped at the same $/MB rate.

Accepts the series id (`polymarket:l2-delta-tape`) as well as the catalog
data_type — see `resolve_raw_identifier`.

parameters.name: shape

schema.description: 'raw' = verbatim venue frames (one `frame` column). 'normalized' = flat per-level depth rows (recv_ts, coin, side, level, price, size, n_orders) — available where a venue normalizer exists (see /raw/datasets).
schema.title: Shape

parameters.description: 'raw' = verbatim venue frames (one `frame` column). 'normalized' = flat per-level depth rows (recv_ts, coin, side, level, price, size, n_orders) — available where a venue normalizer exists (see /raw/datasets).

post.description:
Bulk / multi-series download (T12).

Pull up to 25 datasets in one request. Each line item mirrors a single
GET /v1/download/* call (trades/ohlcv/orderbook by market_id; options/series
by series_id; raw by data_type). We read every item, price the union, apply
the 7-day paid-entitlement waiver per item, then do ONE atomic debit for the
bundle total — all-or-nothing, so a downstream failure never leaves a
partially-charged user (all reads happen before the debit). The response is a
single ZIP: one file per item + a manifest.json. An item with no data in the
requested range is reported empty in the manifest (it does not fail the
bundle). No minimum-order — this is download-shaped, like the single routes.

Create or rotate the auto-provisioned API key for the authenticated user.

Requires a valid Supabase Auth Bearer JWT. The request's email must match
the JWT's email claim — without this check, anyone who knows a user's
email could issue themselves an API key for that account.

Called on every successful login by the web client. Behavior:
- Looks up the authenticated user (the JWT proves they exist in auth.users).
- Revokes any prior auto-provisioned ("Default" / "Auto-provisioned") keys.
- Issues a fresh key and returns its plaintext value.

Custom developer-created keys (any other name) are left untouched so
programmatic access from scripts isn't disrupted by a browser login.

post.description:
Issue a new key with the same name, mark the old one for hard
revocation in 7 days. Gives the caller a window to update their
scripts / cron jobs before the old key stops working.

The 7-day grace is enforced by a daily worker
(services/api-key-maintenance) that hard-revokes any row where
now() > scheduled_revoke_at.

get.description:
Return everything we have on the authenticated user in a single JSON
blob. Satisfies GDPR Art. 15 (right of access) + Art. 20 (portability)
and CCPA right to know in a machine-readable format.

Excludes: api_keys.key_hash (security — exposing a hash is pointless and
risky), email_logs (logged by us, not produced by the user).

The signed-in user's own privacy/security audit trail (C.3) — logins, key
create/revoke/rotate, data exports, deletion requests. JWT-authed and scoped
to the caller's user_id. Returns the SHA-256 `ip_hash` (never the raw IP) and
the user-agent so the dashboard can show "where/when". `privacy_audit_log` is
RLS-locked to service_role, so it's only ever read through this endpoint.

post.description:
Cost preview for a series + date range.

Three counting strategies depending on the series shape:

  1. Crypto-options (Deribit/Lyra/…): sum record_count from
     data_catalog under `{broker}_{ccy}_{product}_{kind}`.
  2. Single-bucket (Kalshi prediction-markets + Polymarket-extras +
     cross-platform + wallet products): same shape as options — one
     parquet per date — but with a different validity matrix.
  3. Polymarket per-market series (the legacy crypto Up/Down + sports
     + politics buckets): sample the underlying markets table and
     scale per-market record counts. Same approach as adding markets
     individually.

get.description:
OHLCV bars for a symbol.

Every failure is reported UDF-style (200 + s="error"), because the charting
library ignores HTTP status codes — a 4xx renders as an empty chart with no
message, which is indistinguishable from "no data" to the user.

schema.title: Response Udf History V1 Charts Udf History Get

get.description:
Ordered trade ticks for a replay window.

ASCENDING by time — replay order. Every other read path in this file sorts
DESC (newest-first, for "latest N"); getting that backwards here would play
the market in reverse, which looks subtly plausible and is completely wrong.

Paginates by CURSOR rather than offset: `next_from` is the timestamp to
resume at, so a long window streams in chunks without the client having to
track how many rows it has already consumed, and without offset paging
drifting as new trades land at the tail.

schema.title: Response Replay Ticks V1 Charts Replay Ticks Get

Submit an export job. Returns 202 with a job handle.

Requires the `download` scope: a job spends money and worker time, so it sits
behind the same permission as a direct download rather than plain `read`.

get.description:
Mint a fresh signed URL for a finished export.

Unmetered and re-issuable: the artifact was already paid for when it was
built, and the durable handle is the job — so a short URL lifetime costs the
customer nothing. This is the capability the 2026-09-02 customer actually
asked for.
API root endpoint.

Public aggregate stats — market/trade counts. No auth required.

Cached in Redis for 5 minutes. The underlying queries are 4 sequential
Supabase REST calls each crossing ~250ms RTT to ap-south-1, so a cache
miss is genuinely expensive (~5–18s); we run them in parallel and stash
the result.

Public health check.

Returns only the overall status ("healthy"/"degraded") + a 200/503 code so a
monitor/load-balancer gets a clean up/down signal without disclosing the
internal component map (audit #8). Detailed component health (DB, fetcher,
cache, recent 5xx) is returned only to callers that present a valid
``X-Health-Token`` (HEALTH_DETAIL_TOKEN) — the uptime-detail probe and
scripts/health-check.sh.
Curated public system status for the status page (no auth).

BulkDownloadItem.title: BulkDownloadItem
BulkDownloadItem.description:
One line item — mirrors a single GET /v1/download/* call.

`kind` selects the dataset family and which id field is required:
  trades / ohlcv / orderbook → market_id (Polymarket markets.id)
  options / series           → series_id
  raw                        → data_type (a raw-capture data_type)

expires_in_days.title: Expires In Days
expires_in_days.description: Optional hard expiry; the key stops authenticating after this many days.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.description: Narrow the key's permissions. Omit for the default (read + download). Pass ['read'] for a browse-only key that CANNOT trigger a paid download. Values outside this closed set are rejected — scopes can only ever reduce a key's power, never extend it.

OrderItemRequest.title: OrderItemRequest
OrderItemRequest.description:
A cart item — either a single market or a whole series.

`series_id` overrides `market_id`: when set, the backend resolves the
series to its underlying markets at checkout time and creates one
download_history row per market (all sharing the same order_id, so they
stay grouped in the Order Center).

`greeks` is only valid for crypto-options series (Deribit, Lyra). The
estimator + download endpoint reject it for Polymarket / futures.
